title: Constants built-in document type: entry shape, anchor-link citation, content comparison against source_of_truth (OPAG-425 R1, R2, R5, R6, R7, R9)
description: Binding record: opum-doc main 7831fff, docs/adr/add-constitution-and-constants-document-types-to-lore.md. Built-in type Constants (slug constants), at most one per bundle (R2), rules in lore check (R3). R5 shape: frontmatter version (SemVer: removing an entry or changing a value is MAJOR, adding one MINOR), last_reviewed (ISO), owner; grouped by level-2 headings; each entry a level-3 heading whose text is its id matching ^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$, unique, never reused, followed by a fixed field list (the exact field syntax is lore-cli's call). Required fields value, meaning, source_of_truth (path#key or this-doc), status (active/deprecated/retired); optional kind, avoid, owner, used_by, replaced_by (required when deprecated, must name an active entry), hot. Descriptive only: facts, never rules or secrets. R6: citing is an ordinary lore link to the entry anchor; check resolves every link into the document and warns on a link to a deprecated entry. R7: where source_of_truth names a JSON, TOML or YAML file and key, the value there must EQUAL value; an unreadable source fails; print entries, comparable sources and references read beside the findings; FAIL when a Constants document exists and zero entries were read (positive control). R9: 'lore new constants' template with one example group and entry and the CODEOWNERS comment.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore check fails a bad id, a duplicate id, a missing required field, a deprecated entry without an active replaced_by, a value that differs from its JSON/TOML/YAML source_of_truth, an unreadable source, and a Constants document from which zero entries were read; it warns on a link to a deprecated entry; each proven by a test
lore check prints the counts of entries, comparable sources and references it read
lore new constants produces a document lore check passes; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: Implemented on branch feat/LCLI-596-constants-type, commit f663bfe0 (not pushed, no PR). DESIGN (lore-cli calls): field syntax is ONE bullet list of "name: value" items directly under each ### entry heading, read as rendered text (bold and code spans contribute their text); HTML comments ignored; any other content under an entry fails. An entry must own its heading slug anchor (the slug drops dots: service.http-port is cited as #servicehttp-port), so an anchor collision is an R5 error. hot is true|false. replaced_by must name an entry in the doc; when deprecated it is required and must be active. R7 renders numbers by JS String(), booleans true/false, null as "null", then exact string equality; YAML under the 1.2 CORE schema; TOML via Bun.TOML, which rejects date-times, so such a file FAILS as unparseable. this-doc, retired entries and non-JSON/TOML/YAML extensions are not compared; the last are counted as notComparableSources. source_of_truth paths are repository-relative (no leading /, no ..) and the reader refuses a symlink that leaves the repo. New check rules: source-of-truth (error), zero-entries-read (error, positive control), deprecated-reference (warning, on the citing file); a missing entry anchor reuses broken-anchor. check.report gains optional readCounts {Constants: {entries, comparableSources, notComparableSources, references}}; human output prints a "Constants read:" line before the summary. TypeRule gains a generic pure bundle facet; the command layer supplies inbound links (core/check.ts linksInto, sharing its resolver with the link gate) and readSource. EVIDENCE: test/constants.test.ts 51 pass. AC1: tests "a bad id", "a duplicate id", "a missing required field" x4, "a deprecated entry without replaced_by", "a value that differs from its JSON/TOML/YAML source_of_truth" (3), "an unreadable source: the file does not exist / does not parse / the key is absent", "a Constants document with groups but no ### entry fails lore check", "a link to a deprecated entry WARNS on the citing file". AC2: "--json carries readCounts", "the human report prints the same counts beside its findings". AC3 partial: "writes a document lore check passes ... even under --strict"; bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings). MUTATION: R7 comparison made always-equal gave exactly 4 of 51 red (3 mismatch tests plus the human-report test, which uses a mismatch as its finding), all R5 tests green; restored, 51 pass. AC3 NOT CHECKED: full bun test is 3686 pass / 1 skip / 3 fail. 2 fails are test/init.test.ts pins (scaffold list needs .lore/schemas/constants.schema.json; skipped.length 14 to 15), a file this task was told not to edit because another open PR changes it. The 3rd is environmental: test/ladybug-version-qualification.test.ts reads <worktree>/node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/package.json and this worktree has no node_modules of its own.

RULINGS (opum-agent ruling 2026-09-26; opum-doc Constants ADR clarification pending): (1) confirmed, R7 skips retired entries and compares active and deprecated ones; new test "a DEPRECATED entry is still compared". (2) extended, a link to a RETIRED entry also warns. Implementation choice: KEPT the single rule name deprecated-reference (no sibling rule), and the message now ends "which is deprecated" or "which is retired", so consumers already filtering on the rule see both. New tests: "a link to a RETIRED entry also warns, saying retired" (warning, exit 0, exit 6 under --strict) and "control: a link to an ACTIVE entry draws no citation warning". MUTATIONS (predicted from the test file before running): M1 drop retired from the warning filter gives exactly 1 of 54 red (the retired-link test); M2 hard-code the word deprecated in the message gives exactly 1 of 54 red (the same test), with the deprecated-link test green; both restored, 54 pass. okf-conformance.md documents both as behaviour, plus the parser limits (TOML date-times rejected as unparseable; integers above 2^53 lose precision). finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#306 (CI pull_request run 36273260495 on 772ac696, plus the closing commit). Built-in Constants type (slug constants) on every OKF version, at most one per bundle (R1, R2). R5 entry shape: ### ids matching ^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$, unique, one "name: value" bullet list per entry, and a deprecated entry needs an active replaced_by. It runs in validate and check alike, and an entry nested in a blockquote or list is an error. R6: citations are anchor links; a missing anchor is broken-anchor, and a link to a deprecated OR retired entry warns (deprecated-reference). R7: a source_of_truth in JSON, TOML or YAML must equal value (source-of-truth). Retired entries are skipped. Every path source must exist, be a regular file inside the repository and be git-tracked, and no finding prints source bytes or parser text. Positive control: zero-entries-read. The additive readCounts field and human output give the entries, comparable sources and references read (AC2). R9: lore new constants passes check --strict. The R6/R7 retired-entry behaviour is bound by opum-doc main f51e8b0 (ODOC-292, Constants ADR Amendment 2). An adversarial review found nothing blocking; S1-S3 and the untested refusals were fixed with mutation evidence (7 of 7 predicted). Behaviour note: path sources need a git checkout, which only affects bundles with a Constants document. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] records the frontmatter key-order effect (0 fleet documents affected).
